reports.title: Ocular Therapeutix™ Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Business Highlights

desk.headline: Revenue down 11% to $12.9m, missed; loss widened to $0.42 a share; AXPAXLI filing still planned for Q4
results: Revenue, all from the eye drug DEXTENZA, fell 11% to $12.9m and came in below the $14.3m estimate.
R&D rose 43% to $74.8m as the HELIOS-3 diabetic retinopathy trial and the SOL-X extension study enrolled faster.
The net loss widened to $94.8m, or $0.42 a share, from $69.4m ($0.38), and was larger than expected.
Cash fell to $530.6m from $737.1m at end-2025, which the company says lasts into 2028.
SOL-R's main efficacy reading was moved to Week 40 from Week 56 so that it happens before the planned Week 52 safety check.

guidance.summary: No revenue or earnings guidance. The company expects cash to last into 2028, plans to file AXPAXLI for wet AMD with the FDA in Q4 2026, and expects SOL-R topline results in Q1 2028.

watch: Whether the AXPAXLI application is filed in Q4 2026 and accepted for review by the FDA.
Results of the interim SOL-R Week 52 safety analysis.
Further declines in DEXTENZA sales and rising launch costs, which the runway does not fully cover.
